questions.question: In the Zurich release, what new capability allows developers to work in isolated environments and merge changes using Git?

explanation.correct: Developer Sandboxes are now generally available in Zurich, allowing each developer to spin up an isolated sandbox environment tied to the same base development instance. Sandboxes are integrated with Git for branching, commits, and merges.

wrongAnswers.A: Update Set Batching is not a new Zurich feature for isolated development.
wrongAnswers.C: Instance Cloning creates full copies of instances, not isolated developer environments with Git integration.
wrongAnswers.D: Application Scoping existed before Zurich and doesn't provide isolated development environments.

questions.question: Which Zurich feature enables ServiceNow to integrate with CI/CD systems like Jenkins or GitHub Actions for automated builds and deployments?

explanation.correct: Build Agents in Zurich integrate ServiceNow apps and flows with CI/CD systems. They manage builds, tests, and deployments automatically, replacing manual update set promotion.

wrongAnswers.A: Flow Designer Triggers handle workflow automation, not CI/CD integration.
wrongAnswers.B: ReleaseOps provides governance and release pipelines but Build Agents handle the actual CI/CD integration.
wrongAnswers.D: Update Set Pipelines is not a Zurich feature name.

questions.question: What new trigger type was added to Flow Designer in the Zurich release that allows external systems to initiate flows?

explanation.correct: Zurich adds external REST/webhook triggers to Flow Designer. Previously, flows were limited to internal events (record changes, schedules). Now external systems can fire flows via webhooks.

wrongAnswers.A: Scheduled Triggers existed before Zurich, though reusable schedules are new.
wrongAnswers.B: Record-based Triggers existed in previous releases.
wrongAnswers.D: Email Triggers are not a new Zurich feature.

questions.question: In Zurich, which new Flow Designer capability allows you to define a schedule once and reuse it across multiple flows?

explanation.correct: Zurich introduces Reusable Scheduled Triggers. Instead of creating a 'run nightly at 2 AM' trigger multiple times, you can define a schedule once and reuse it everywhere.

wrongAnswers.A: Shared Actions are for reusable flow actions, not schedules.
wrongAnswers.C: Flow Templates are not the specific Zurich feature for schedule reuse.
wrongAnswers.D: Subflow Libraries existed before; this question is about schedule reuse.

questions.question: What debugging improvement in Zurich allows administrators to trace data transformations step-by-step in failed flows?

explanation.correct: Zurich introduces detailed Flow Run History and debugging tools. You can view each execution, see which conditions passed or failed, and trace data transformations step by step.

wrongAnswers.A: Script Debugger is for server-side scripts, not Flow Designer debugging.
wrongAnswers.C: System Logs provide general logging but not the step-by-step flow tracing.
wrongAnswers.D: Application Logs don't provide the Flow Designer-specific debugging view.

questions.question: Which visual enhancement was added to Studio and Builder tools in the Zurich release based on developer feedback?

explanation.correct: Dark Mode across dev tools was one of the most requested features. Zurich implements Dark Mode in Studio, Flow Designer, and other development tools to reduce eye strain during long sessions.

wrongAnswers.A: High Contrast Mode is an accessibility feature, not the specific Zurich addition.
wrongAnswers.C: Compact View is not the highlighted Zurich visual enhancement.
wrongAnswers.D: Full Screen Mode is not the new Zurich feature.

questions.question: What new capability in Zurich allows Now Assist to support multiple large language models including OpenAI and Anthropic?

explanation.correct: Zurich expands Now Assist with Multi-LLM Support, allowing organizations to use multiple large language models including Azure OpenAI, Claude, and Gemini.

wrongAnswers.A: LLM Connector is not the official Zurich feature name.
wrongAnswers.B: AI Model Selection is not the correct term for this capability.
wrongAnswers.D: Generative AI Hub is not the specific Zurich feature name.

questions.question: Which Zurich feature provides structured release pipelines with automated quality checks and policy enforcement?

explanation.correct: ReleaseOps in Zurich provides structured release pipelines with automated quality checks, real-time dashboards, and policy enforcement to meet compliance standards.

wrongAnswers.A: Update Set Validator checks update sets but doesn't provide full release pipeline governance.
wrongAnswers.C: Deployment Manager is not the Zurich feature name.
wrongAnswers.D: Change Advisory Board (CAB) is a process, not a Zurich automation feature.
